title: Blog
text: I found orientation really informative and fun. Except from hearing about how intense the program was, I learnt a lot about networking, future events, and what is expected from this program overall. Alongside this, the ice breakers were really fun - particularly day 2. The bonding from the strange activities we were told to do around campus definitely formed a lot of friendships. I think this was extremely well planned and helped us dive into the program smoothly.

title: Blog
text:
First Week
The first week of classes definitely hit us hard. The workload was definitely eye opening and I’m sure it forced a lot of us to actually put our heads down and lock in. I learnt how to effectively keep track of the millions of things we have due each week by forcing myself to buy a planner for the first time in years. Although it was rough, at least we now know what to expect for the rest of the program.

title: Blog
text:
Looking ahead
Although the workload is rough, I still am looking forward to how much we will end up learning throughout this program. I am also lookign forward to my new role as the Academic Representative for Section 001, where I will get to know the students and professors more.

title: Nidhi Danda
text:
Hi! I’m Nidhi Danda and I grew up in Malawi (lake Malawi shown above - the most beautiful place ever, I’m not biased I promise). I did my Bachelors in Chemistry here at UBC and graduated in May 2026. By pursuing my Masters in Data Science, I hope I can build my Computation and Quantum Chemistry skills that I gained during my last two years of research.
This is a Quarto website.
To learn more about Quarto websites visit https://quarto.org/docs/websites.

title: About
text: I was born in Kenya but I moved to Malawi when I was two and lived there my whole life - so I consider Malawi home. I then moved to Vancouver in 2022 after high school to study Chemistry here at UBCV and graduated in May 2026. During my undergraduate degree, I pursued research in Quantum, Theoretical, and Computational Chemistry, creating a perfect pathway to start the MDS program.

title: About
text:
Why Data Science?
My previous undergraduate research heavily involved Machine Learning, building a bridge between Chemistry and Data Science. However, majority of my previous experience was self taught. I struggled quite a bit during my research due to no actual machine learning guidance (no classes or anyone to teach me). Because of this, I decided a Masters in Data Science would significantly improve my skills and open up numerous opportunities in the future.

title: About
text:
About me!
Moving to Vancouver was the perfect decision for someone who has the hobbies I do. I absolutely love running; I ran the BMO Vancouver marathon and it was a beautiful route that allowed you to see the entire city. I also love hiking, which is what I am constantly doing throughout the very few months of good weather in Vancouver.
